reuse.why: The rule change and the API field both go through the existing shared getExpectedScheduleAmount, but the parallel older getScheduledAmount (used by the UI) and schedule-template's inline midpoint are left untouched.

duplication.why: The diff itself adds no copied logic; it keeps the rule in one function, though it leaves the pre-existing parallel helper and inline midpoint copy un-consolidated.

placement.why: The rule stays in shared/schedules.ts and the API field is computed in the API model layer via that helper.

scope.why: Only the helper, its callers that need the operator, the API model and tests are changed.

maintainability.why: The approximate rule depends on each caller remembering to pass op (forecast-schedules and the API do not), and other paths still compute amounts with a different helper, so the 'expected amount' differs across the app.

abstraction_drift.where: getExpectedScheduleAmount gains an optional op parameter and an 'isapprox' branch; budget/schedule-template.ts keeps its own midpoint and desktop-client callers keep using the separate getScheduledAmount (still midpoint); forecast-schedules.ts and api-models.ts call the helper without op.
